items.text: When people explain their own decisions, their stated reasons are:

options.A: Usually accurate reflections of actual causes
options.B: Often accurate with occasional blind spots
options.C: Partially accurate, with significant blind spots
options.E: Mostly post-hoc rationalizations of unconscious processes

items.text: An executive explains her career choice as "intellectual fulfillment." A psychologist suggests it's really about unresolved childhood needs. Which is more "real"?

options.A: Her conscious explanation—people know their own minds
options.B: Conscious reasons are primary, unconscious factors secondary
options.C: Both can be true simultaneously and are equally real
options.D: Unconscious factors are primary, conscious reasons secondary
options.E: The unconscious explanation—people rarely know their true motives

items.text: Freud claimed the unconscious drives most behavior; cognitive scientists emphasize rational information processing. Who's closer to truth?

options.A: Cognitive scientists—humans are primarily rational agents
options.B: Cognitive science captures more, with unconscious as secondary
options.C: Both capture important aspects—reason and unconscious intertwine
options.D: Freud captures more, with rationality as secondary
options.E: Freud—unconscious forces drive most human behavior
